section: Humidity, evaporation, condensation, clouds and forms of precipitation
subsections: Clouds → appearance and altitude class, rain-bearing clouds, cloud-seeding chemicals
Instruments and isolines → what they measure or join

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes cirrus clouds?
o: Dark, thick clouds producing steady rainfall at low altitude
Towering clouds with an anvil-shaped top producing hail
Grey-blue clouds found at middle altitude with continuous rainfall
Thin, feathery and silky clouds found at high altitude
accepted.x: Cirrus clouds are high-altitude clouds with a thin, feathery and silky appearance.
accepted.tq: Use the appearance–altitude association to distinguish closely related cloud types.
accepted.sec: Clouds → appearance and altitude class, rain-bearing clouds, cloud-seeding chemicals  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding high-altitude clouds:
1. Cirrostratus appears as a thin, milky sheet.
2. Cirrocumulus consists of small globular masses or ripples.
3. Cirrostratus is associated with the formation of a halo.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Cirrostratus is a thin milky sheet that can produce a halo, while cirrocumulus consists of small globular masses or ripples. All three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Match each cloud’s visual feature with its distinctive atmospheric effect before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Clouds → appearance and altitude class, rain-bearing clouds, cloud-seeding chemicals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The term ‘mackerel sky’ is associated with which one of the following cloud types?
accepted.x: Cirrocumulus clouds form small globular masses or ripples commonly referred to as a mackerel sky.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive descriptive name to separate visually similar cloud families.
accepted.sec: Clouds → appearance and altitude class, rain-bearing clouds, cloud-seeding chemicals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Altostratus — grey or bluish even sheet
Cumulus — dark shapeless layer with continuous rain
accepted.x: Altostratus appears as a grey or bluish even sheet. Globular masses describe cirrocumulus, dark thick layers describe nimbostratus, and cauliflower heaps describe cumulus.
accepted.tq: Eliminate options by comparing each cloud’s stated appearance with its standard description.
accepted.sec: Clouds → appearance and altitude class, rain-bearing clouds, cloud-seeding chemicals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Nimbostratus clouds are generally found at which level and are associated with which weather condition?
o: High level; fair weather without rainfall
Vertical level; short afternoon convectional showers only
Low level; dark, thick clouds producing steady continuous rain
accepted.x: Nimbostratus is a low-level, dark and thick cloud layer that produces steady, continuous rain.
accepted.tq: Link the base height, appearance and rainfall pattern instead of relying on one feature alone.
accepted.sec: Clouds → appearance and altitude class, rain-bearing clouds, cloud-seeding chemicals  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to cumulus clouds, consider the following statements:
1. They generally have a heaped, cauliflower-like form.
2. They usually have a flat base.
3. They are associated with fair weather but may grow into cumulonimbus clouds.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Cumulus clouds have heaped cauliflower tops and generally flat bases. They are commonly associated with fair weather but can develop vertically into cumulonimbus clouds.
accepted.tq: Check whether the statements describe the complete life and appearance of a cumulus cloud.
accepted.sec: Clouds → appearance and altitude class, rain-bearing clouds, cloud-seeding chemicals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Cumulus clouds are commonly associated with which approximate altitude range?
accepted.x: The approximate altitude range given for cumulus clouds is 4,000–7,000 metres.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the approximate altitude range of cumulus from the standard high, middle and low cloud classes.
accepted.sec: Clouds → appearance and altitude class, rain-bearing clouds, cloud-seeding chemicals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about cumulonimbus clouds is correct?
o: They are low, shapeless clouds producing only light drizzle.
They are middle-level clouds through which the Sun appears like ground glass.
They are towering clouds that may extend up to about 15 km and have an anvil-shaped top.
They are thin, silky clouds restricted to the upper troposphere.
accepted.x: Cumulonimbus clouds have marked vertical development, may reach about 15 km, and commonly have a towering anvil-shaped top.
accepted.tq: Use the extreme vertical extent and anvil top as decisive identifiers.
accepted.sec: Clouds → appearance and altitude class, rain-bearing clouds, cloud-seeding chemicals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The word ‘nimbus’ in cloud terminology indicates that the cloud is
accepted.x: ‘Nimbus’ denotes a rain-bearing cloud or a cloud associated with precipitation.
accepted.tq: Test the precise meaning of a technical word rather than its general visual appearance.
accepted.sec: Clouds → appearance and altitude class, rain-bearing clouds, cloud-seeding chemicals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following chemicals is principally used in cloud seeding because its crystal structure resembles that of ice?
accepted.x: Silver iodide is used in cloud seeding because its crystal structure mimics that of ice and assists ice-crystal formation.
accepted.tq: Apply the material–function association used in atmospheric modification.
accepted.sec: Clouds → appearance and altitude class, rain-bearing clouds, cloud-seeding chemicals  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about cloud seeding:
1. Silver iodide, dry ice and common salt may be used as cloud-seeding agents.
2. Cloud seeding can produce rainfall even when suitable clouds are completely absent.
3. Silver iodide is useful because its crystal structure mimics that of ice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Silver iodide, dry ice and common salt may be used for cloud seeding, and silver iodide resembles ice crystallographically. Cloud seeding requires suitable supercooled clouds already to exist; it cannot work in their complete absence.
accepted.tq: Spot the false absolute claim about cloud seeding and retain the two mechanism-based statements.
accepted.sec: Clouds → appearance and altitude class, rain-bearing clouds, cloud-seeding chemicals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which instrument is used to determine the moisture or humidity present in the air?
accepted.x: A hygrometer measures moisture or humidity in the air. A hydrometer measures the density of a liquid.
accepted.tq: Separate the look-alike terms hygrometer and hydrometer by their measured quantities.
accepted.sec: Instruments and isolines → what they measure or join  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A sling psychrometer determines atmospheric humidity primarily by using
o: rainfall depth and wind speed readings
accepted.x: A sling psychrometer estimates humidity from the difference between wet-bulb and dry-bulb temperatures.
accepted.tq: Identify the instrument from the pair of observations required for its operation.
accepted.sec: Instruments and isolines → what they measure or join  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: An isobar joins places of equal atmospheric pressure, not equal temperature. An isotherm joins places of equal temperature.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped meaning in the pair of commonly confused isolines.
accepted.sec: Instruments and isolines → what they measure or join  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding wet-bulb temperature is correct?
o: It is always higher than the dry-bulb temperature.
It is equal to the dry-bulb temperature only when relative humidity is zero.
It is independent of relative humidity.
It is the lowest temperature air can reach through evaporation.
accepted.x: Wet-bulb temperature is the lowest temperature that air can attain through evaporation. It equals dry-bulb temperature when relative humidity is 100 percent.
accepted.tq: Use the definition and limiting condition to reject reversed temperature statements.
accepted.sec: Instruments and isolines → what they measure or join  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At 100 per cent relative humidity, the wet-bulb temperature is
o: lower than the dry-bulb temperature by 10°C
accepted.x: When air is fully saturated, no further evaporative cooling occurs, so wet-bulb and dry-bulb temperatures are equal.
accepted.tq: Use the saturation limit to identify the correct relationship between paired measurements.
accepted.sec: Instruments and isolines → what they measure or join  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Above approximately which temperature can the human body fail to cool itself effectively through sweating, according to the given atmospheric relationship?
accepted.x: Above approximately 31.5°C, the body cannot cool itself effectively through sweating under the stated condition.
accepted.tq: Pay attention to the threshold value rather than confusing it with ordinary body or air temperatures.
accepted.sec: Instruments and isolines → what they measure or join  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The rain gauge described in the Mauryan Arthashastra measured rainfall in terms of which unit?
accepted.x: The Mauryan Arthashastra described a state rain gauge whose measurement was expressed in drona, approximately 13.2 kg of water.
accepted.tq: Link the historical instrument with its distinctive unit rather than with a modern rainfall unit.
accepted.sec: Instruments and isolines → what they measure or join  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The approximate quantity represented by one drona of water in the Mauryan rain-gauge description is
accepted.x: One drona in the cited description represented approximately 13.2 kg of water.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact historical figure from nearby distractor values.
accepted.sec: Instruments and isolines → what they measure or join  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following rain-gauge milestones in chronological order:
A. Castelli’s rain gauge
B. Rain gauge described in the Mauryan Arthashastra
C. Korea’s Cheugugi
Which one of the following is the correct sequence?
accepted.x: The Mauryan Arthashastra description predates Korea’s Cheugugi of 1441, which in turn predates Castelli’s rain gauge of 1639.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest historical reference first and then place the dated instruments in sequence.
accepted.sec: Instruments and isolines → what they measure or join  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes convectional precipitation?
o: Moist air is forced up a mountain slope and descends dry on the leeward side.
Warm air is lifted over cold air along a front.
Strong surface heating causes air to rise, cool and condense, often producing afternoon showers.
Rainfall results exclusively from the movement of ocean currents.
accepted.x: Convectional precipitation develops when intense heating causes air to rise, cool and condense, commonly producing afternoon showers and thunderstorms.
accepted.tq: Identify the precipitation type from its initiating mechanism rather than its location alone.
accepted.sec: Precipitation types - convectional, orographic, cyclonic/frontal  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Equatorial regions may receive convectional rain almost every day throughout the year.
2. Pre-monsoon mango showers are an example of convectional precipitation.
3. Convectional precipitation is caused by warm air being lifted over cold air along a front.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Equatorial daily rainfall and pre-monsoon mango showers are examples of convectional precipitation. Warm air rising over cold air along a front describes frontal precipitation, not convectional precipitation.
accepted.tq: Separate heating-driven uplift from frontal uplift when evaluating the statements.
accepted.sec: Precipitation types - convectional, orographic, cyclonic/frontal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Orographic precipitation occurs when
o: air rises only because of intense heating over an ocean
cold air sinks below warm air in the lower atmosphere
dry air descends on the windward slope of a mountain
moist air is forced to rise over a mountain barrier
accepted.x: Orographic precipitation results when moist winds are forced upward over a mountain or other relief barrier.
accepted.tq: Identify the relief-based mechanism and distinguish it from convectional and frontal uplift.
accepted.sec: Precipitation types - convectional, orographic, cyclonic/frontal  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to orographic rainfall, consider the following statements:
1. The windward side of a mountain generally receives heavier rainfall.
2. The leeward side may lie in a rain shadow.
3. Agumbe and Hulikal are associated with the wet Western Ghats.
4. Rayalaseema lies in the rain-shadow region in the stated monsoon setting.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Moist air produces heavier rainfall on the windward side, while the leeward side is drier. Agumbe and Hulikal are wet Western Ghats locations, and Rayalaseema is identified as lying in the rain shadow in the stated setting.
accepted.tq: Combine the physical rule with the location-based examples before selecting the complete code.
accepted.sec: Precipitation types - convectional, orographic, cyclonic/frontal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following locations is identified as the driest place in India, with approximately 8.33 cm of rainfall?
accepted.x: Ruyli in Jaisalmer is identified as the driest place in India, receiving approximately 8.33 cm of rainfall.
accepted.tq: Use the location–rainfall extreme pair and distinguish the dry extreme from wet-region examples.
accepted.sec: Precipitation types - convectional, orographic, cyclonic/frontal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The rainfall at Mawsynram is most directly associated with which type of precipitation?
o: Frontal precipitation caused by western disturbances
Cyclonic precipitation caused only by temperate cyclones
accepted.x: Mawsynram receives exceptional rainfall due primarily to the orographic lifting of moist winds over relief.
accepted.tq: Apply the relief mechanism to a well-known high-rainfall location.
accepted.sec: Precipitation types - convectional, orographic, cyclonic/frontal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Cyclonic or frontal precipitation is best described as precipitation in which
o: warm air is lifted over cold air along a front or air rises in a cyclone’s low-pressure centre
moist air descends on the windward side of a mountain
air rises only after intense heating over an equatorial landmass
rainfall is produced exclusively by cloud seeding
accepted.x: Cyclonic or frontal precipitation occurs when warm air rises over cold air along fronts or when air rises in a cyclone’s low-pressure centre.
accepted.tq: Match the precipitation type with its defining uplift mechanism and avoid absolute distractors.
accepted.sec: Precipitation types - convectional, orographic, cyclonic/frontal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Western disturbances — 10–15 cm winter precipitation in north-western India
Mango showers — frontal precipitation in temperate belts
Ruyli — wettest location of the Western Ghats
accepted.x: Western disturbances can provide about 10–15 cm of precipitation to north-western India, benefiting rabi crops. The other pairs reverse or misstate the geographical associations.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive rainfall amount and then eliminate reversed location–phenomenon pairs.
accepted.sec: Precipitation types - convectional, orographic, cyclonic/frontal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the context of the south-west monsoon, which of the following regions is identified as lying in its rain shadow?
o: Only the windward slopes of the Western Ghats
Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and the interiors of Tamil Nadu
Only the coastal districts of Kerala
accepted.x: After crossing the Western Ghats, the stated rain-shadow region includes Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and the interiors of Tamil Nadu.
accepted.tq: Use the windward–leeward relationship to identify the grouped rain-shadow regions.
accepted.sec: Precipitation types - convectional, orographic, cyclonic/frontal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the examples of precipitation types?
o: Equatorial afternoon showers—cyclonic; Western Ghats rainfall—convectional; Bay of Bengal cyclones—orographic
Equatorial afternoon showers—convectional; Western Ghats rainfall—orographic; Bay of Bengal cyclones—cyclonic
All three examples represent frontal precipitation
Equatorial afternoon showers—orographic; Western Ghats rainfall—cyclonic; Bay of Bengal cyclones—convectional
accepted.x: Equatorial and summer-interior afternoon showers are convectional, Western Ghats rainfall is orographic, and Bay of Bengal cyclones produce cyclonic precipitation.
accepted.tq: Classify each example by its initiating mechanism rather than by the amount of rainfall.
accepted.sec: Precipitation types - convectional, orographic, cyclonic/frontal  [APPSC]
